description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between TFLOPs (trillion floating-point operations) on the x-axis and Loss Ratio (%) on the y-axis for four variants of the SepLLM model, as evaluated in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis is logarithmic, ranging from 1e7 to 9e8 TFLOPs with major ticks at 1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 5e8, 1e9, and 2e9 (though labeled only up to 9e8), while the y-axis is linear, spanning from 94% to 100% Loss Ratio with tick marks every 1%. Five lines are plotted: a purple line with triangle markers labeled “SepLLM (n=64)” starts near 99.9% and remains nearly flat across the TFLOP range; an orange line with circle markers for “SepLLM (n=128)” begins at ~98.3% and rises to ~100.1% before stabilizing; a blue line with cross markers for “SepLLM (n=64, H)” starts at ~97.3%, rises to ~99.9%, and fluctuates slightly around 99.8–100.0%; a green line with diamond markers for “SepLLM (n=64, H)” begins at ~97.7%, peaks near 100.0% around 3e8 TFLOPs, and remains close to 100%; and a red line with circle markers for “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” starts at 94.0%, climbs steeply to ~98.7% by 5e7 TFLOPs, peaks at ~99.1% around 4e8 TFLOPs, then dips to ~98.5% before leveling off near 98.7%. All lines exhibit increasing or stable loss ratios with higher computational cost, with the red line showing the lowest initial performance and the purple line the highest and most stable.
